subject.title: [Feature]: Add a visible browser panel to the Control UI for login handoff and browser management

question: Should the browser login handoff surface ship as a first-party Control UI panel now, as a browser-plugin Control UI tab using the current descriptor seam, or wait for the broader plugin UI entry-point API?
rationale: The remaining work crosses UX, browser-auth exposure, plugin/core ownership, operator scopes, and resume-policy boundaries; source inspection shows primitives exist, but automation cannot safely choose the permanent product and security boundary.

options.title: First-party read-only-first panel
options.body: Build a core-owned admin-scoped Control UI browser page for status, tabs, URL/title, screenshots/logs, and explicit resume, with separate gates for clicks, credential fields, and submit actions.

options.title: Browser plugin tab
options.body: Have the bundled browser plugin register a Control UI tab and keep the panel plugin-owned, using current or near-term descriptor APIs with a security-reviewed iframe/update model.

options.title: Wait for entry-point API
options.body: Defer implementation until the broader plugin UI entry-point contract lands, then implement browser handoff as the first security-reviewed consumer of that contract.

recommendation.title: First-party read-only-first panel
recommendation.body: Build a core-owned admin-scoped Control UI browser page for status, tabs, URL/title, screenshots/logs, and explicit resume, with separate gates for clicks, credential fields, and submit actions.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest combined signal from the canonical issue comment and recent browser-runtime work.
